title.en: M. Hamel and the last lesson

hook.en: For forty years M. Hamel taught in one village school. Today he must say goodbye, and he does it with great dignity.

objectives.en: Describe M. Hamel's character and his farewell
Explain whom he blames for neglect of learning
Trace the change in Franz during the lesson

narration.en: For forty years M. Hamel taught in one village school. Today he must say goodbye, and he does it with great dignity.

body.en: M. Hamel is strict but devoted. On the last day he is patient and calm and teaches with great feeling. He tells the class that French is a beautiful, clear and logical language, and that a people who keep their language hold a kind of key to their freedom even when conquered. He also admits his own share of blame for neglecting lessons.

points.en: Forty years of service in the same school
Praises French as clear and logical
Blames parents, pupils and himself for putting off learning

narration.en: M. Hamel is strict but devoted. On the last day he is patient and calm and teaches with great feeling.
Let us map the people in M. Hamel's classroom on the last day.

say.en: At the centre is M. Hamel, the teacher who has served the village for forty years.
Franz is the narrator. He arrives late and is soon full of regret.
Old Hauser, an elder, has come with an old primer and reads along.
Other villagers, like the former mayor and postmaster, sit at the back to show respect.
The youngest children practise their letters and syllables.
Outside, the Prussian soldiers and their trumpets stand for the new rulers.

narration.en: The events in the classroom, retold in our own words. Put them in order.

prompt.en: Put the events of the last lesson in order.

steps.en: Franz cannot say the rule for participles
M. Hamel does not scold him; Franz's shame is punishment enough
M. Hamel praises French as clear and logical
He says a people who keep their language hold a key to freedom
He admits his own share of blame
Franz listens as never before and finds the grammar clear
The clock strikes twelve and Prussian trumpets sound
Too moved to speak, M. Hamel writes on the board and dismisses the class

explanation.en: Franz's change of heart comes on the very day the chance to learn is taken away.

body.en: When Franz cannot say the rule for participles, M. Hamel does not scold him; the shame he feels is punishment enough. Suddenly his books seem like old friends, and he understands his teacher. He listens as never before and finds the grammar lesson clear. When the clock strikes twelve and the Prussian trumpets sound, M. Hamel, too moved to speak, writes a patriotic message on the board and dismisses the class.

points.en: From careless pupil to attentive learner
Books turn from a burden into old friends
Writing lesson, history lesson and the little ones' alphabet
Ending: noon, the Prussian trumpets, a silent farewell

body.en: M. Hamel says everyone put off learning: Parents sent children to work, Pupils said there was always tomorrow, and the Teacher himself gave holidays and sent pupils on errands.

problem.en: Describe the character of M. Hamel as revealed in the last lesson.

steps.en: Introduce him: a teacher who served the village school for forty years.
Show his strictness earlier and his gentleness and patience on the last day.
Show his love for French and his message about language and freedom.
Mention his honesty in blaming himself, and his emotional, silent farewell.

answer.en: M. Hamel is a dedicated, strict but loving teacher whose patriotism and honesty shine on his last day. He teaches with unusual patience, praises French, admits his own faults, and ends with a silent, dignified farewell.
